Project 01 · Poultry utilization

Improving wooden breast breakfast sausage with citrus fiber.

Lead researcher and presenting author

Breakfast sausage · Rheology · Texture · Sensory quality
The challenge

Wooden breast meat can be undervalued because altered protein functionality creates processing, texture, and water management problems.

The approach

Formulated breakfast sausage with normal and severe wooden breast meat, with and without citrus fiber, then evaluated batter behavior, cooking performance, objective texture, and trained sensory response.

What the evidence showed

Citrus fiber improved cooking yield and changed batter and product texture. It reduced hardness in patties containing 50 percent wooden breast meat with limited effects on the broader sensory profile.

Practical relevance

A clean label formulation strategy may help convert a lower value poultry raw material into a more functional further processed product.

Commercial poultry collectionBench and pilot processingDynamic rheologyTexture profile analysisTrained sensory panelCooking yield

Project 02 · Product quality

Using citrus fiber to improve wooden breast chicken nuggets.

Lead researcher and presenting author

Chicken nuggets · Water holding capacity · Texture · Sensory analysis
The challenge

Wooden breast can diminish water holding capacity and texture while creating substantial value loss for poultry processors.

The approach

Produced nuggets with three wooden breast inclusion levels and evaluated citrus fiber through cooking yield, texture, shear, proximate composition, and sensory analysis.

What the evidence showed

Fiber improved cooking yield by 6.4 to 8.9 percent across inclusion levels and mitigated important texture differences without broadly changing flavor attributes.

Practical relevance

The results support further processed nuggets as a potential value recovery pathway for wooden breast meat.
